root_cause.text: In the DRM TTM swapout path, ttm_bo_swapout_cb() incorrectly reinserted a resource into bulk_move/LRU after ttm_tt_swapout() failure by moving it to the LRU tail while an LRU walk hitch cursor still sat after the yielded entry, causing the walker to encounter the same resource again and loop forever.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states that on swapout failure the code called ttm_resource_add_bulk_move() and ttm_resource_move_to_lru_tail(), and that moving the resource to the LRU tail placed it "in front of" the hitch node so the next list_for_each_entry_continue() found the same resource again, causing an infinite loop; the patch removes the pre-swapout del/re-add logic and only deletes bulk_move membership on the success path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update swapout handling to adjust LRU and unevictable bulk-move state only after successful TT swapout.
intent_record.what: The code removes the pre-swapout LRU lock section that called ttm_resource_del_bulk_move(bo->resource, bo), removes the post-swapout logic that re-added the resource on failure with ttm_resource_add_bulk_move(bo->resource, bo), and replaces it with a conditional block that runs only when ttm_tt_swapout() succeeds, taking bdev->lru_lock and calling ttm_resource_del_bulk_move_unevictable(bo->resource, bo) followed by ttm_resource_move_to_lru_tail(bo->resource).
intent_record.how: At runtime, the buffer object's resource is no longer removed from bulk-move tracking before attempting swapout and is no longer conditionally restored on failure. Instead, LRU/bulk-move state is updated only after a successful swapout, which avoids unnecessary state churn on failure and ensures unevictable bulk-move bookkeeping is cleared only when the object was actually swapped out and then moved to the LRU tail.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a special bulk-move removal helper to delete resources that have just become unevictable while warning if the state is unexpected.
intent_record.what: A new function, ttm_resource_del_bulk_move_unevictable(struct ttm_resource *res, struct ttm_buffer_object *bo), was added along with a comment explaining its purpose. The function emits WARN_ON_ONCE if !ttm_resource_unevictable(res, bo) and, if bo->bulk_move is non-NULL, calls ttm_lru_bulk_move_del(bo->bulk_move, res). Unlike the existing ttm_resource_del_bulk_move(), it does not gate removal on an unevictable check.
intent_record.how: This adds a way to remove a resource from a bulk_move list even after the buffer object has become unevictable, while asserting that the resource is in that expected state. At runtime, it prevents resources from remaining incorrectly tracked in bulk_move ranges solely because the normal deletion path would skip removal once unevictable status changed.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a new public API to remove TTM resources from bulk-move tracking for unevictable buffer objects.
intent_record.what: A new function declaration, `ttm_resource_del_bulk_move_unevictable(struct ttm_resource *res, struct ttm_buffer_object *bo);`, was added to the header alongside the existing bulk-move resource management APIs.
intent_record.how: This exposes a new callable interface for removing a resource from bulk-move handling specifically for the unevictable case, enabling other code to invoke distinct unevictable-removal behavior at runtime where previously only the generic delete function was declared.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it delays LRU/bulk-move and unevictable state adjustments until after successful TT swapout, preventing the erroneous reinsertion/move on swapout failure that could make the LRU walker revisit the same resource and loop indefinitely.

The root cause is incorrect reinsertion into bulk_move/LRU after swapout failure, which causes the LRU walker cursor to revisit the same resource and loop forever. This change instead adds a helper to remove resources that became unevictable and warn on unexpected state; it does not address the swapout failure reinsertion/walker-cursor interaction.

This change adds an API for removing unevictable resources from bulk-move tracking, but the root cause is a swapout/LRU walk bug where a failed swapout reinserts a resource and causes the walker to revisit it indefinitely. The new API does not directly fix that reinsertion/hitch-cursor looping logic.

candidates.rationale: This unconditional LRU tail move executes even when ttm_tt_swapout() fails. Moving the yielded resource while the LRU walk cursor is positioned after it causes the walker to encounter the same resource again, leading to the infinite loop described in the root cause.

This condition shows the failure path where the resource is specially handled after swapout failure. It gates reinsertion into bulk_move, which is part of the erroneous post-failure state restoration that contributes to the bad LRU walk behavior.

On swapout failure, this reinserts the resource into bulk_move/LRU-related tracking before success is established. Combined with the LRU tail move, it embodies the incorrect reinsert-after-failure behavior mentioned in the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement is the direct cause of the vulnerability. It unconditionally moves the yielded resource to the LRU tail even when ttm_tt_swapout() has failed, which repositions the entry behind the LRU walk hitch cursor and allows the walker to encounter the same resource again indefinitely.

The root cause was that on `ttm_tt_swapout()` failure the code reinserted the resource into bulk_move/LRU by moving it to the LRU tail while the LRU walk hitch cursor was positioned after the yielded entry, allowing the walker to see the same resource again. In this commit, before swapout the code explicitly removes the resource from bulk_move under `lru_lock`: `ttm_resource_del_bulk_move(bo->resource, bo);`. After `ret = ttm_tt_swapout(...)`, it does `if (ret) ttm_resource_add_bulk_move(bo->resource, bo);` and then `ttm_resource_move_to_lru_tail(bo->resource);`. This matches the commit message's v4 note: `Don't move to LRU tail during swapout until the resource is properly swapped or there was a swapout failure.` That indicates the earlier vulnerable behavior was moving during swapout before outcome was known; this version delays the move until after swapout completes or fails. Also, the new `ttm_bo_populate()` restores swapped objects to the proper LRU only when they transition back from swapped state: `if (swapped && !ttm_tt_is_swapped(tt) && !bo->pin_count && bo->resource) { ... ttm_resource_add_bulk_move(...); ttm_resource_move_to_lru_tail(...); }`, which is consistent with the fix described in the commit message. Therefore the vulnerable construct is not present here, and the fix is already included.
